accepted.question_text: Let S_m be the space of real 2 x m matrices, let L_1 and L_2 be self-adjoint positive-definite linear maps on S_m, let F_1,F_2 in S_m and c_1,c_2 in R define the two quadratic wells W_j(F)=(F-F_j)·L_j(F-F_j)+c_j, and let W(F)=min{W_1(F),W_2(F)}. Is the quasiconvex envelope QW of this two-well energy always equal to its rank-one convex envelope RW in two spatial dimensions, for every choice of m,L_1,L_2,F_1,F_2,c_1,c_2?

evidence.quote: Problem 1: Is rank convexity equal to quasiconvexity for the two well problem in two spatial dimen- sions?

accepted.question_text: Consider a two-phase composite in two spatial dimensions in which phase 1 occupies volume fraction f, the right-hand fields are n-tuples of fields each equal to a constant real 2-vector plus the gradient of a scalar periodic potential, the left-hand fields are n-tuples of divergence-free fields, and the constitutive law is J(x)=L(x)E(x) with L(x)=chi(x)L_1+[1-chi(x)]L_2. Is the G_f-closure of all achievable effective tensors L* equal to the closure obtained using only multiple-rank laminate microstructures, for every positive integer n?

evidence.quote: Problem 2: For two-phase composites in two spatial dimensions, such that phase 1 occupies a volume fraction f, is the Gf -closure equal to its lamination closure when the fields on the right of the constitutive law have n components, each being the sum of a real 2 component vector and the gradient of a scalar periodic potential, while the fields on the left of the constitutive law also have n components, each having zero divergence, in which n is an arbitrary positive integer?

accepted.question_text: Take a three-dimensional isotropic composite built from two isotropic materials with scalar conductivities sigma and 1, and suppose the composite remains isotropic with effective conductivity sigma*(sigma) I. Which scalar functions sigma*(sigma) can occur as the effective conductivity function of such composites?

evidence.quote: Problem 3: For three-dimensional isotropic composites each having an effective conductivity σ∗I and being built from two isotropic materials having conductivities σI and I, can one characterize all possible conductivity functions σ∗(σ)?

accepted.question_text: For three-dimensional isotropic composites made from two isotropic phases, are all effective conductivity functions sigma*(sigma) realizable by multiple-rank laminate microstructures? If the answer is yes, is it enough to use laminate constructions in which each lamination step is taken only along mutually orthogonal directions?

evidence.quote: Problem 4: For three-dimensional isotropic composites of two isotropic phases, are all possible conductivity functions σ∗(σ) achievable by multiple rank laminate microstructures and, if so, does it suffice to consider laminate microstructures where one laminates only in mutually orthogonal directions?

accepted.question_text: Let sigma(x)=chi(x) sigma_1 + [1-chi(x)] sigma_2 describe a two-dimensional periodic composite of two anisotropic phases with anisotropic 2 x 2 conductivity tensors sigma_1 and sigma_2, and let sigma*(sigma_1,sigma_2) be its effective conductivity tensor. Can every effective conductivity function sigma*(sigma_1,sigma_2) achievable by such composites also be achieved by a multiple-rank laminate microstructure?

evidence.quote: Problem 5: For two-dimensional anisotropic composites of two anisotropic phases, are all possible conductivity functions σ∗(σ1,σ2) achievable by multiple rank laminate microstructures?

accepted.question_text: For isotropic two-phase composites with complex effective permittivity, some known geometries place the effective permittivity on a particular bounding circular arc in the complex plane and can therefore attain maximal absorption in the quasistatic limit. Are there other microgeometries with isotropic effective permittivities whose effective responses also lie on that same arc?

evidence.quote: Problem 6: Are there other geometries with isotropic effective permittivities that lie on the arc?

accepted.question_text: Several known microgeometries maximize absorption for isotropic two-phase composites, including coated-disk and coated-sphere assemblages and certain multiple-rank laminates. Can any of these maximum-absorption geometries be replaced by simpler geometries, ideally periodic ones with only one inclusion per unit cell, while preserving the same optimal absorption behavior?

evidence.quote: Problem 7: Can any of these discovered geometries, having maximum absorption, can be replaced by simpler ones?

accepted.question_text: Take a composite formed by mixing an isotropic elastic phase with either a void phase or a rigid phase. Can one completely characterize the resulting G-closure, that is, the full set of effective elasticity tensors obtainable from all such microstructures?
accepted.context_brief: elastic G-closure with void or rigid phase

evidence.quote: Problem 8: Can one complete the characterization of the G-closure for a void (or rigid) phase mixed with an isotropic elastic phase?

accepted.question_text: For an isotropic composite made from one elastic phase and void, let kappa* and mu* denote the effective bulk and shear moduli and let kappa and mu be the moduli of the solid phase. The elementary bounds imply mu* - c kappa* <= mu for every c>0. Can this inequality be sharpened in two and/or three dimensions for some range of c>0, or equivalently can one construct composites whose effective moduli approach the limiting pair (kappa*,mu*)=(0,mu)?
accepted.context_brief: shear versus bulk tradeoff with voids

evidence.quote: Problem 9: The bounds (4.1) imply µ∗ − cκ∗ ≤ µ for all c > 0. Can this inequality be improved, in 2 and/or 3 dimensions, for a range of c > 0? Alternatively, can one construct composites of an elastic phase with void with (κ∗, µ∗) arbitrarily close to (0, µ)?

accepted.question_text: Fix c>0. Among isotropic composites made from an elastic phase and void, which microstructures in two and/or three dimensions maximize the quantity mu* - c kappa*, or at least form a sequence of microstructures whose values of mu* - c kappa* converge to the supremum?
accepted.context_brief: optimal auxetic objective for fixed c

evidence.quote: Problem 10: Identify, for given c > 0, in 2 and/or 3 dimensions, isotropic microstructures of an elastic phase with void that have the largest possible value of µ∗ − cκ∗ (or a sequence of isotropic microstructures with moduli such that µ∗ − cκ∗ converges to its largest possible value).

accepted.question_text: In two dimensions, consider elastic materials built from one elastic phase and void, and impose the limiting incompressible/auxetic condition kappa*=0 together with 1/kappa=0 for the solid phase. Is 4 mu / 5 the largest possible effective shear modulus mu* under these constraints?

evidence.quote: Problem 11: Is 4µ/5 the largest possible value of µ∗ for a two-dimensional elastic material with voids, given that κ∗ = 1/κ = 0?

accepted.question_text: When deformations are finite but still small enough that nonlinear geometric effects matter, can one derive bounds that relate the achievable compressive deformations and shear deformations of composites made from an elastic phase and void, rather than relying only on infinitesimal linearized moduli?

evidence.quote: Problem 12: Can one obtain bounds that correlate the possible compressive and shear deformations of composites when these deformations are not infinitesimal?

accepted.question_text: For three-dimensional isotropic elastic polycrystals obtained by combining differently oriented grains of a single crystal, what pairs (kappa*,mu*) of effective bulk and shear moduli are achievable? In particular, can one characterize the full feasible region beyond the currently sharp bulk-modulus bounds and the known but non-optimal shear-modulus bounds?

evidence.quote: Problem 13: What are the possible (κ∗, µ∗)-pairs for three-dimensional isotropic elastic polycrystals (composites built from a single crystal in various orientations)?

accepted.question_text: For isotropic composites made from two isotropic elastic phases, with one phase possibly rigid or void, can one derive bounds on the achievable effective bulk and shear modulus pairs (kappa*,mu*) that improve on the current best-known inequalities, and ultimately determine the optimal bounds exactly?

evidence.quote: Problem 14: Can one obtain improved bounds on the elastic moduli pairs of isotropic composites of two isotropic elastic phases, and ultimately find the optimal ones?

trace.notes: Mapped the paper 'Some open problems in the theory of composites' (28 pages). Major sections are: 1 Introduction; 2 Open problems involving quasiconvexification; 3 Some open problems related to the effective conductivity as a function of the component conductivities; 4 Bounds on the elastic moduli of an elastic material with voids, and the ultimate auxetic material in this class of materials; 5 Some future directions for wave and other equations; followed by references. Explicit numbered problem statements occur in sections 2-4 and are the main high-confidence extraction targets.
Section 2 yields explicit candidates q_001 and q_002 from the numbered open problems on quasiconvexification and G-closure versus lamination closure.
Section 3 yields explicit candidates q_003 through q_007 from the numbered conductivity and absorption-geometry problems.

Section 5 contains several future research directions in waves, Q*-convexity, neutral inclusions, Green's functions, and time-domain bounds, but these are mostly implicit rather than numbered.
